mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in unemployment, signals a positive supply shock that will boost productivity and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 0.5% in 1 month, and UNRATE does not rise > 0.2pp
failure_condition: SPX realizes negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, if it exceeds a 0.5% threshold over 3 months, signals a weakening labor market that will drag on consumer spending and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises > 5 points during the signal period, contradicting the weakening labor market signal.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening yield curve, as measured by the 10y-2y spread, signals impending monetary tightening that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve steepens by > 20bps during the signal period, reversing the tightening signal.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts, if accompanied by a contemporaneous decline in the unemployment rate, signal a strengthening consumer sector that will boost S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 5% YoY, and UNRATE declines > 0.3pp in 3 months
failure_condition: Consumer sentiment (UMich index) falls > 10 points during the signal period, contradicting the positive consumer signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the federal funds rate, if it exceeds a 0.5% threshold over 3 months, signals a tightening monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Real M2 money supply growth accelerates > 5% YoY during the signal period, indicating ongoing monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial capacity utilization, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in inflation, signals a negative supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 1% YoY, and CPIAUCSL does not rise > 0.5pp
failure_condition: SPX realizes positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating payroll growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in nonfarm payrolls, signals a strengthening labor market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims rise > 10% YoY during the signal period, contradicting the positive labor market signal.
